propositions: Code review currently lacks a concurrency criterion for race detection; security and performance overlays cover specific attack/load patterns but not general correctness races.

A two-tier deterministic lexical trigger (committed high-precision token-based + project-extensible noisy vocabulary) enables portable race detection that fires on explicit synchronization primitives and project-specific patterns.

The committed tier deliberately does not fire on unlocked-twin races (raw git rm/commit, getmtime-then-remove patterns); project-tier vocabulary in .rebar/criteria_routing.json bridges this recall gap for modal races in specific repos.
The concurrency overlay ships advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) and must be registered in the base reviewer catalog so Pass-2 verifier disciplines can escalate findings.
Projects can extend built-in overlay triggers and `applies_to` globs through .rebar/criteria_routing.json without code changes, enabling customization of race detection scope and vocabulary.
